_doc: France, the Low Countries, the German-speaking Alps and Central Europe.

destinations.name: Paris
destinations.blurb: Still the benchmark: the Louvre, the boulevards, the bistros and the bakeries — best in the shoulder seasons when the queues thin out.

destinations.name: Nice & the Côte d'Azur
destinations.blurb: A long pebble bay under palm trees, an Italianate old town, and Monaco, Antibes and Saint-Tropez strung along the coast beside it.
photos: Nice old town Cours Saleya market

destinations.name: Provence
destinations.blurb: Lavender rows, hilltop villages, Roman aqueducts and rosé — with the mistral wind and, in July, an awful lot of company.

destinations.name: Chamonix
destinations.blurb: Under the summit of Mont Blanc: serious off-piste in winter, serious alpinism in summer, and a town that never pretends otherwise.

destinations.name: Corsica
destinations.blurb: 'The mountain in the sea': granite peaks, the brutal GR20 trek and some of the Mediterranean's most beautiful and least built-up beaches.

destinations.name: Bordeaux
destinations.blurb: A honey-stone 18th-century city that cleaned itself up beautifully, surrounded by the most famous vineyards on earth.
photos: Place de la Bourse water mirror Bordeaux

destinations.name: Lyon
destinations.blurb: France's gastronomic capital, with Renaissance secret passageways, two rivers and the Alps ninety minutes away.
photos: Basilica Notre Dame de Fourviere Lyon

destinations.name: Brittany
destinations.blurb: Celtic France: granite ports, megalithic stones, tidal islands and crêperies — cooler and wilder than the south, and far cheaper.

destinations.name: Berlin
destinations.blurb: Europe's most restless capital: brutal 20th-century history, the best club scene in the world, and still cheap for a major city.

destinations.name: Munich
destinations.blurb: Beer halls, superb galleries and river surfing in a park bigger than Central Park — with the Alps an hour south.

destinations.name: Bavarian Alps
destinations.blurb: Neuschwanstein, painted villages and Germany's highest peak — gentler and cheaper skiing than the big Alpine names.

destinations.name: Black Forest
destinations.blurb: Dense fir forest, cuckoo clocks, thermal spa towns and a surprising density of Michelin stars along a famous scenic drive.

destinations.name: Hamburg
destinations.blurb: More bridges than Venice and Amsterdam combined, a spectacular concert hall, red-brick warehouses and a famously rowdy harbour quarter.

destinations.name: Amsterdam
destinations.blurb: Canal rings, Rembrandt and Van Gogh, and a bike-first city centre — beautiful, tolerant, and openly tired of stag parties.

destinations.name: Bruges
destinations.blurb: A perfectly preserved medieval merchant town of canals, belfries and Flemish primitives — plus the best beer and chocolate in Europe.

destinations.name: Vienna
destinations.blurb: Imperial palaces, the world's great concert halls and coffee houses you can occupy for hours — repeatedly voted the most liveable city on earth.

destinations.name: Salzburg
destinations.blurb: Mozart's baroque hometown under a hilltop fortress, with the Sound of Music lakes and the Alps starting at the edge of town.

destinations.name: Tyrol & Innsbruck
destinations.blurb: A city with a ski jump in it and mountains on all four sides — two Winter Olympics, and lift access straight from the old town.

destinations.name: Hallstatt & the Salzkammergut
destinations.blurb: The most photographed village in Austria, wedged between a mirror lake and a cliff, in a region of 76 lakes and salt mines.

destinations.name: Zermatt
destinations.blurb: Car-free, under the Matterhorn, with skiing possible 365 days a year on the glacier. Superb, and priced for people who know it.

destinations.name: Interlaken & the Jungfrau
destinations.blurb: Between two lakes below the Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau — Europe's adventure-sport capital and the highest railway station on the continent.

destinations.name: Lucerne
destinations.blurb: A covered wooden bridge, a painted old town and a lake ringed by mountains you can ride cogwheel trains up. Switzerland's greatest hits.

destinations.name: Zurich
destinations.blurb: A banking city that swims in its own river, with excellent galleries, a serious club scene and the highest prices in Europe.

destinations.name: Prague
destinations.blurb: A gothic and baroque city that came through the war intact — spires, a castle, the world's cheapest great beer, and enormous crowds.
photos: Prague old town square astronomical clock

destinations.name: Český Krumlov
destinations.blurb: A tiny medieval town looped by a river beneath an enormous castle — a day trip from Prague that deserves an overnight.

destinations.name: Budapest
destinations.blurb: Grand Habsburg boulevards, thermal baths built like palaces, and ruin bars in derelict courtyards — outstanding value for a capital.

destinations.name: Kraków
destinations.blurb: Poland's beautiful old capital — Europe's largest medieval market square, the Jewish quarter of Kazimierz, and Auschwitz an hour away.
photos: Krakow Main Market Square Cloth Hall

destinations.name: Gdańsk
destinations.blurb: A rebuilt Hanseatic merchant city on the Baltic — amber, extraordinary WWII and Solidarity museums, and beaches on the tram line.

destinations.name: Warsaw
destinations.blurb: Rebuilt from rubble and now unmistakably confident — a meticulously reconstructed old town beside glass towers and a serious food scene.
photos: Palace of Culture and Science Warsaw
